inhalt:
The **Arlberg** is a legend. No other ski resort in Austria combines so much world-class excellence in such a compact space: **305 kilometers** of groomed runs, **over 200 kilometers** of deep-snow routes, **88 modern lift installations**, and four exclusive mountain villages, each with its own distinct personality. **St. Anton** pulses with energy, **Lech** sparkles with elegance, **Zürs** exudes exclusivity, and **Stuben** offers a tranquil charm. Together, they form the **Arlberg region**—the cradle of alpine skiing and, to this day, one of the world’s best ski destinations. In this article, you’ll find everything you need to know for the perfect ski holiday at the **Arlberg**: from the best descents and après-ski hotspots to practical tips on travel, accommodation, and budgeting.

---

## **The Arlberg Ski Region – Numbers, Facts & Figures**

The **Arlberg** stretches around the namesake pass at **1,793 meters** elevation, connecting the Austrian states of **Tirol** and **Vorarlberg**. Since the merger of the individual resorts **St. Anton, St. Christoph, Stuben, Zürs**, and **Lech** in 2016, the **Arlberg ski area** has become Austria’s largest contiguous ski region.

**Key figures at a glance:**
- **Piste kilometers:** 305 km (139 km blue, 117 km red, 49 km black)
- **Deep-snow routes:** Over 200 km
- **Lift installations:** 88 (29 cable cars & gondolas, 30 chairlifts, 29 drag lifts)
- **Highest point:** Vallugagrat at **2,811 meters**
- **Lowest point:** St. Anton at **1,304 meters**
- **Vertical drop:** Up to **1,507 meters**
- **Ski season:** Early December to late April (main season mid-December to mid-April)
- **Snow reliability:** Thanks to high altitude and snowmaking on over **85%** of the slopes, it’s very high

The **Arlberg region** spans five distinct villages. **[St. Anton am Arlberg](/orte/st-anton/)** is the undisputed center with **10,500 residents** and the highest density of hotels, restaurants, and après-ski bars. **Lech am Arlberg** is the luxurious counterpart, featuring five-star hotels, exclusive chalets, and a quieter yet equally elegant atmosphere. **Zürs** is the most exclusive and traditional village in the region—an international jet-set hotspot for over 100 years. **St. Christoph** lies directly at the **Arlberg Pass** and is home to the legendary **Arlberg Hospiz Hotel**. **Stuben** is the smallest and most authentic village, perfect for those seeking peace and genuine charm.

---

## **St. Anton – The Heart of the Arlberg**

**St. Anton am Arlberg** is more than just a ski resort—it’s an institution. Over more than 100 years, the village has transformed from a quiet mountain hamlet into an international ski metropolis. **Hannes Schneider**, who taught modern skiing here in the 1920s, is considered one of the fathers of alpine skiing. His techniques spread from **St. Anton** across the globe.

Today, **St. Anton** is the epicenter of **Arlberg** ski culture. Several lifts depart directly from the village. The **Galzig (2,185 m)** is **St. Anton’s** home mountain and the starting point for countless descents. The **Vallugabahn** takes experienced skiers up to **2,811 meters**—either with a controlled descent (guided only) or the legendary **Run 1** down to **Zürs**. The **Rendl (2,038 m)** is famous for its perfectly groomed slopes, fun park, and popular Thursday night skiing. The **Gampen (1,842 m)** is the ideal beginner mountain for families and leisure skiers.

**Our favorite runs in St. Anton:**
- **Run 1 from the Valluga:** Absolute legend—**5.7 km** through untouched deep powder down to **Zürs**. Only with a guide and avalanche gear (cost: ~€35 per person for the tour).
- **Karl-Schranz Run:** One of the Alps’ most beautiful red runs—**7 km** from the **Galzig** down to **St. Anton**.
- **Mattun Run:** Deep-snow classic for experts—challenging terrain off the groomed slopes.
- **Schindlerkar:** Another deep-snow highlight with extremely steep slopes and deep powder.

For adrenaline seekers, the **Funpark Rendl** offers one of **Tirol’s** best snowboard and freeski parks, featuring boxes, rails, and kickers for all levels.

---

## **Lech & Zürs – Deep Powder & Pure Luxury**

While **St. Anton** is known for its vibrant energy, **Lech** and **Zürs** represent a different kind of alpine excellence: luxury, discretion, and first-class service. **Lech am Arlberg** has been repeatedly named Austria’s most beautiful ski village. The famous **Lech-Zürs Loop**, a **22 km** ski tour through the entire area, is the heart of the skiing experience.

**Zürs** has a special history: As early as the 1930s, European nobility discovered the small village as a ski destination. The **Zürserhof Hotel**, opened in 1927, remains one of Europe’s most exclusive ski hotels today. The **Rote Wand**, **Zürs’** home mountain, offers challenging descents and one of the Alps’ most stunning viewpoints.

**Highlights in Lech & Zürs:**
- **Lech-Zürs Loop:** **22 km**, **6 lifts**, **5 descents**—a must for every skier.
- **Warth-Schröcken:** Since 2013, connected to the **Arlberg** via the **Auenfeldjet-Bahn**—a **7 km** pendulum lift, one of the world’s most modern.
- **Trittkopf:** **Lech’s** home mountain with wide, sunny slopes and breathtaking panoramas.
- **Rüfikopf:** Overlooking **Lech**, featuring steep descents and the famous **Panoramarestaurant**.

**Lech** is also renowned for its gastronomy. Many huts and restaurants are awarded with stars or Michelin bibs. **Hus Nr. 8** in **Zürs** and **Alpe Rauzböden** are two particularly recommended addresses for regional cuisine at the highest level.

---

## **Après-Ski & Culinary Delights – From the Hut to the Luxury Lounge**

The **Arlberg** boasts one of the Alps’ most legendary après-ski scenes. **St. Anton** leads the way: the two most famous spots are the [**Mooserwirt**](/gastro/mooserwirt) and the [**Krazy Kanguruh**](/gastro/krazy-kanguruh)—both located right on the slopes, both meeting points for skiers from around the world for decades. Here, people dance on benches, beer is served in one-liter mugs, and the party goes on until the last run.

But the **Arlberg** offers far more than just party vibes. The [**Alpengasthof Arlberg**](/gastro/alpengasthof-arlberg) in **St. Anton** serves traditional **Tiroler** cuisine with homemade bacon and cheese. The **Fuxegg** on the **Galzig** is famous for its **Kaiserschmarrn** variations. The **Ulmer Hütte** at **2,226 meters** offers one of the most beautiful sun terraces and is affectionately called the “most beautiful hut on the **Arlberg**.”

For gourmets, the **Arlberg** is a paradise. The **Halde** restaurant in **Lech** (at the **Hotel Bergkristall**) holds two Michelin stars and offers a creative take on alpine cuisine. The **Sennhütte** in **Zürs** serves Austrian classics with refined touches—their **Käsnock’n** are, according to many guests, the best on the **Arlberg**.

**Typical Après-Ski Opening Hours:**
- [**Mooserwirt**](/gastro/mooserwirt/): daily from **1:00 PM** to **8:00 PM** (longer in peak season)
- [**Krazy Kanguruh**](/gastro/krazy-kanguruh/): daily from **1:00 PM** to **7:30 PM**
- **Fangalm:** Cozier après-ski with live music from **2:00 PM**
- **Underground** (pizzeria in **St. Anton** center): partying until the early morning hours

**Important tip:** If you’re looking for a quiet ski trip, avoid the main season between Christmas and New Year’s, as well as the February school holidays. Alternatively, the first two weeks of December and March are ideal—less crowded with the same snow quality.

## **Prices, Ski Passes & Savings Tips**

A ski holiday at the **Arlberg** is pricey—comparable to the Alps’ top ski resorts. The quality, however, fully justifies the cost.

**Ski Pass Prices (Season 2025/26 – Estimates):**
| Ticket | Main Season | Off-Season |
|---|---|---|
| Adult Day Pass | ~€72 | ~€63 |
| Youth Day Pass (2006–2009) | ~€57 | ~€50 |
| Child Day Pass (2010–2018) | ~€36 | ~€32 |
| Adult 6-Day Pass | ~€370 | ~€325 |
| Season Pass | ~€1,590 | – |

**Savings Tips for Ski Passes:**
- Book passes online at [www.skiarlberg.at](http://www.skiarlberg.at) – up to **10% early-bird discount**.
- The **Arlberg Inclusive Pass** includes ski/snowboard rental, lunch, and drinks (from **€145/day**).
- Afternoon tickets (from **12:30 PM**) are cheaper and ideal for last-minute decisions.
- Children born in **2019 or later** ski free (with a paying parent).

**Ski Rental (Daily Rates – Estimates):**
- Beginner Set (skis + boots + poles): from **€35**
- Premium Set (brand skis, e.g., **Atomic, Head**): from **€55**
- Snowboard Set: from **€40**

Ski schools are available in every village. A group lesson costs around **€70–90/day** (4 hours), private lessons from **€120/hour**. Particularly recommended: the **Arlberg Ski School** in **St. Anton**—one of the oldest and most prestigious ski schools in the world.

## **Accommodations at the Arlberg – From Luxury Hotels to Mountain Huts**

The **Arlberg region** offers lodging for every taste and budget. In **[St. Anton](/regionen/arlberg)**, you’ll find everything from budget pensions to five-star luxury hotels. **[Lech](/regionen/arlberg)** sets the highest standards with numerous four- and five-star hotels, while **[Zürs](/regionen/arlberg)** excels in absolute exclusivity.

**Our Recommendations by Category:**

**Luxury (over €400/night):**
- **Hotel Arlberg Hospiz** (**St. Christoph**) – Legendary five-star hotel at the **Arlberg Pass** with wellness and gourmet dining.
- **Zürserhof** (**Zürs**) – One of Europe’s most exclusive alpine hotels, family-owned since 1927.
- **Hotel Kristiania** (**Lech**) – Boutique hotel with a Michelin-starred restaurant, member of the **Leading Hotels of the World**.

**Mid-Range (€150–400/night):**
- **Hotel Senn** (**St. Anton**) – Central four-star hotel with sauna and village views.
- **Posthotel Lech** – Traditional four-star hotel with a modern spa.
- **Hotel Traube** (**St. Anton**) – Family-run, central location, great value for money.

**Budget (under €150/night):**
- **Pension Alte Post** (**St. Anton**) – Simple but clean rooms in a central location.
- **Youth Hostel St. Anton** – Ideal for groups and young travelers.
- **Gästehaus Schneider** (**Stuben**) – Small breakfast pension with a warm atmosphere.

**Important Tip:** During peak season (Christmas to New Year’s, February holidays), accommodations are often booked weeks or months in advance. Reserve your lodging as early as possible—ideally by **October** for Christmas and by **November** for the spring season.

## **Travel, Parking & Local Mobility**

The **Arlberg** is exceptionally well-connected. Whether by car, train, or plane, getting there is straightforward.

**By Car:**
The **Arlberg Schnellstraße (S16)** runs directly through the region. From **Innsbruck**, it’s about **100 km (1.5 hours)**, from **Munich** around **200 km (2.5 hours)**, and from **Zürich** roughly **230 km (3 hours)**. **Note:** The **Arlberg Pass** is often snow-covered in winter—**snow chains are recommended**, and winter tires are mandatory. The **Arlberg Tunnel (S16)** bypasses the pass year-round without snow.

**By Train:**
The **St. Anton** train station is on the **Arlbergbahn** (route **Innsbruck–Bludenz–Zürich**). The **Railjet** stops multiple times daily. From **Innsbruck**, it’s about **1 hour 20 minutes**, from **Vienna** around **5 hours**, and from **Zürich** approximately **3.5 hours**. Many hotels offer free shuttle service from the station.

**By Plane:**
The nearest airports are **Innsbruck (INN, 100 km)**, **Friedrichshafen (FDH, 110 km)**, and **Zürich (ZRH, 210 km)**. From **Innsbruck Airport**, the **Arlberg Express** (bus) goes directly to **St. Anton**—about **1 hour 45 minutes**.

**Parking:**
In **St. Anton**, there are several paid parking garages (around **€12–18/day**). In **Lech** and **Zürs**, parking is also paid, but many hotels offer free parking for guests.
